questions.q:
In how many of the following molecules/ions, the number of electrons in $\sigma$ molecular orbital (both $\sigma \& \sigma$ ) are more than or equal to 9 . (In ground state)
(a) $\mathrm{N}_2$
(b) $\mathrm{N}_2^{+}$
(c) $\mathrm{Be}_2^{+}$
(d) $\mathrm{B}_2^{-}$
(e) $\mathrm{B}_2$
(f) $\mathrm{C}_2^{2-}$
(g) $\mathrm{C}_2$
(h) $\mathrm{H}_2$
(i) $\mathrm{Li}_2^{+}$
(j) $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$
(k) $\mathrm{F}_2^{+}$
questions.solution:
$\because \quad$ for molecules upto $\mathrm{N}_2, \sigma 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 \sigma^* 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 \sigma 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 \sigma^* 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 \pi 2 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{x}}^2=$ $\pi 2 p_y^2 \sigma 2 p_z^2$ order is followed.
Hence in
(a) $10 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(b) $9 e^{-}$
(c) $7 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(d) $8 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(e) $8 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(f) $10 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(g) $8 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(h) $2 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
(i) $5 \mathrm{e}^{-}$
are present

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.examName: Most Important Selected Qs for JEE Advanced
questions.q: The number of equivalent contributing structures possible for $\mathrm{XeO}_6^{4-}$ is m . The bond order of $\mathrm{Xe}-\mathrm{O}$ bond is $n$. Find $(m \times n) \times 0.2$. Round off your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.solution:
Bond order of $\mathrm{XeO}_6^{4-}$ is $4 / 3=n$
It has 15 possible structures $\therefore \quad m=15$ Thus $\mathrm{mn}=15 \times \frac{4}{3}=20 \quad \therefore \quad 0.2 \mathrm{mn}=0.2 \times 20=4$

questions.q: Among the following species ${N}_{2}, {N}_{2}^{+}, {N}_{2}^{-}, {N}_{2}^{2 -}, {O}_{2}, {O}_{2}^{+}, {O}_{2}^{-}, {O}_{2}^{2 -}$ the number of species showing diamagnetism is
questions.solution:
The molecules with unpaired electrons are paramagnetic and molecules with all electrons paired are diamagnetic. In general molecules with an even number of electrons (except $10$ and $16$ electrons) are diamagnetic

$\begin{cases}{N}_{2} & 14{e}^{-}\end{cases}diamagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{N}_{2}^{+} & 13{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{N}_{2}^{-} & 15{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{N}_{2}^{2 -} & 16{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{O}_{2} & 16{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{O}_{2}^{+} & 15{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{O}_{2}^{-} & 17{e}^{-}\end{cases}paramagnetic$

$\begin{cases}{O}_{2}^{2 -} & 18{e}^{-}\end{cases}diamagnetic$

questions.q:
The number of molecule(s) or ion(s) from the following having non-planar structure is______.

${NO}_{3}^{-}, {H}_{2}{O}_{2}, {BF}_{3}, {PCl}_{3}, {XeF}_{4}$,

${SF}_{4}, {XeO}_{3}, {PH}_{4}^{+}, {SO}_{3}, {\left[Al{\left(OH\right)}_{4}\right]}^{-}$
questions.solution:
The species which have ${sp}^{2}$ hybridisation with no lone pairs, ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ hybridisation with two lone pairs are planar molecules.

The number of hybrid orbitals can be calculated as follows,

No.of hybrid orbitals = 1/2(V+M-C+A)

V = number of valence electrons

M = number of monovalent atoms attached to central atom.

C = Number of positive charges on the molecule

A = Number of negative charges on the molecule

${SO}_{3}$ ${sp}^{2}$ Planar
${BF}_{3}$ ${sp}^{2}$ Planar
${NO}_{3}^{-}$ ${sp}^{2}$ Planar
${SF}_{4}$ ${sp}^{3}d$ Non-Planar
${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$ ${sp}^{3}$ Non-Planar
${PCl}_{3}$ ${sp}^{3}$ Non-Planar
${\left[Al{\left(OH\right)}_{4}\right]}^{-}$ ${sp}^{3}$ Non-Planar
${XeF}_{4}$ ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ Planar
${XeO}_{3}$ ${sp}^{3}$ Non-Planar
${PH}_{4}^{+}$ ${sp}^{3}$ Non-Planar
